bottom_line: Sanctions-evasion risk is shifting toward intermediary routing through Central Asia and Caspian trade corridors, with partial but actionable evidence; quantitative attribution remains weak.
what_changed: Trade-flow anomalies and AML/CFT typology updates point to growing use of corridor intermediaries; OFAC and FATF materials provide official context but not corridor-level volumes.
why_it_matters: Compliance and sanctions teams need to update screening, beneficial-ownership checks, and counterparty risk models to cover routing layers that previously were not primary risk areas.
affected_actors: multinationals operating in Central Asia / Caspian
main_uncertainty: Beneficial ownership and exact corridor volumes are not transparent; aggregate trade data is lagged and noisy.

scenarios.name: Sustained corridor shift
scenarios.description: Routing shift consolidates; new typologies and designations follow.
indicators: new OFAC designations naming corridor intermediaries
FATF typology updates referencing the region

scenarios.name: Tactical reversal
scenarios.description: Pressure on intermediaries pushes routing elsewhere within months.
indicators: spike then drop in corridor-related designations

watch_next: New OFAC and EU designation records mentioning corridor intermediaries
FATF publications on regional AML/CFT typologies
UN Comtrade flow anomalies for the corridor
